newsitem.title: SPAIN: Banesto sets new banking division.
newsitem.headline: Banesto sets new banking division.

text.p: Spain's Banesto bank said it had created a new banking division as part of an effort to boost sluggish areas of business as its two-year restructuring programme draws to a close.

"Banesto has created a wholesale banking division that will bring together those areas of business which have a high potential but which have not been fully stimulated," the bank said in a note published late on Friday.
The new division will incorporate corporate banking, capital markets, international banking and private banking.
The bank -- taken over by Banco Santander SA in 1994 -- said its heavy restructuring programme would be concluded by the end of the year and it was now embarking on a relaunch of all its businesses.
Chairman Alfredo Saenz imposed a tough rationalisation regime designed to rid the troubled bank of huge bad debts and non-strategic assets when he was appointed in 1994.

The company said the results of the rationalisation were already reflected in growth in its traditional areas of commercial banking and an improvement in results which it expected to extend into 1997.
"The bank has defined various objectives for 1997 whose completion will guarantee the continuation of the current trend in results obtained since 1994," the bank said.
From losses of 12 billion pesetas in 1994, the bank said it had achieved profits of 21 billion pesetas in 1995, and around 23 billion peseta pretax profit for the first nine months of 1996.
Within the new banking division, Banesto said the Corporate banking unit would open new specialist offices around Spain to gain a greater presence among big companies.
It added that it would also focus on promoting the activities of its stock market unit, Banesto Bolsa.
